html:
Retained answers and Agent Check policy flows

Retaining an answer and accepting completion are separate operations. The runtime can preserve a model's final text while showing why its terminal claim was rejected. Reevaluation checks the accepted task, current evidence and applicable policies; the presence of answer text never establishes that a tool ran successfully.

An explicit Agent Check change has two recovery surfaces. A general run override uses the check owner's resume strategy and can re-admit a proved unexecuted tool candidate without another model call. The completion-only compatibility endpoint reevaluates an exact retained answer without dispatching tools. Both preserve the original evidence and use native run ownership.

Checks and authority owns check categories and authority boundaries. Completion normalization owns terminal declaration validation and deterministic receipt-backed normalization. This guide connects retained text, scoped policy storage, recovery and publication.

Retained text and its acceptance identity

flowchart TD Decision[Accepted assistant decision] --> Classify[inspect_message] Classify -->|Plain response or sole finish_task| Text[Nonempty final message or assistant content] Classify -->|Plan, mixed executable calls or legacy function_call| Exclude[No final-response candidate] Text --> Intent{Continuation request?} Intent -->|Yes| Exclude Intent -->|No| Journal[Canonical assistant journal] Journal --> Candidate[Candidate references journal index and decision identity] Metadata[Allowlisted terminal metadata and parse reasons] --> Candidate Revision[Evidence and intent revision, stream completeness] --> Candidate Candidate --> Present[Retained text and feedback projection] Candidate --> Evaluate[Local acceptance evaluation] Journal --> Emit[Post-commit ordered presentation chunks] Evaluate --> Accepted[Ordinary terminal acceptance or rejection state] Accepted --> Publish[Trace, conversation and current-run publication] Present --> Publish

final_response.inspect_message accepts plain assistant content or a sole finish_task control outside Plan mode. It prefers a nonempty finish_task.message over introductory assistant content. Mixed tool calls, legacy function_call and empty content do not become candidates. Malformed terminal metadata can still accompany preserved answer text; its error codes remain available for validation.

retain excludes continuation prose using the ordinary terminal-control validator. Each accepted model decision has one candidate identity (run_id:calls). The candidate stores a journal index, stream-completeness flag, parse reasons, selected terminal metadata and completion revision. It does not duplicate the answer body. When retaining a rejected wrapper before journal append, it appends plain assistant content so provider history does not acquire an orphan tool-call group.

The caller commits the journal before emit_retained emits ordered 768-character chunks. A presentation-emitted marker is independent of completion acceptance. presentation can return retained text and feedback even when its revision is no longer current. relevant and the acceptance/recovery callers own that freshness decision. A displayed answer is therefore evidence of retained content, not of terminal success.

Local reevaluation and rejected completion

flowchart TD Start[Evaluate retained candidate] --> Current{Relevant, unrejected and no new amendment?} Current -->|No| Leave[Leave candidate acceptance to normal progression] Current -->|Yes| Wait{Outstanding waits or runtime fault?} Wait -->|Yes| Owner[Existing wait or fault owner decides state] Wait -->|No| Complete{Stream complete?} Complete -->|No| Partial[Keep interrupted answer and partial feedback] Complete -->|Yes| Validate[Validate control intent, research and terminal metadata] Validate --> Normalize[Check frozen output and real completion prerequisites] Normalize -->|Accepted| Finish[Apply ordinary terminal outcome] Normalize -->|Rejected| Feedback[Preserve text, feedback and rejected candidate] Validate -->|Invalid control or metadata| Recovery[Bounded normal correction path] Feedback --> Recovery Finish --> Facts[Accepted marker, verification facts and events] Recovery --> Boundary[Calling owner decides continued work or suspension]

Evaluation itself performs no model request or tool dispatch. It first respects deferred work, current candidate revision and unconsumed amendments. Successful completion intent passes through the background-work gate and runtime-fault owner before presentation checks. An interrupted stream remains partial rather than being promoted to success.

The ordinary terminal-control and research validators still apply. Strict structure checking distinguishes missing bookkeeping that can be normalized locally from invalid terminal metadata that needs the bounded correction path. Output-contract, model-citation and receipt checks retain their own guard flags. A frozen output contract is not replaced by a later contradictory declaration.

Incomplete terminal statuses use validate_incomplete. Successful intent goes through normalize_terminal_response, output validation and, when the model declared evidence/checks or a different terminal status, explicit completion validation. Declared evidence is not silently replaced by another receipt bundle. Accepted completion updates the ordinary terminal owner and clears obsolete recovery/feedback fields.

Failure preserves the answer and records feedback, a rejected-candidate marker and the relevant guard strike/recovery state. The normal loop may then need a bounded correction decision. A local reevaluation's zero model-call count does not promise that the surrounding task will never need another decision.

Save global or conversation policy

sequenceDiagram actor Person participant API as Guard settings route participant Queue as Task-queue lock participant Authority as Shared RAM or attached SQLite participant Tasks as Unstarted chat tasks participant Views as UI update broker Person->>API: Set or reset a scoped guard API->>API: Validate conversation when supplied API->>Queue: Acquire queue lock API->>Authority: Begin authority transaction API->>Authority: Set boolean or delete inherited override opt Conversation completion-structure policy only Authority->>Tasks: Update eligible queued tasks in same transaction Tasks->>Tasks: Record policy checkpoints and advance lane versions end Authority-->>API: Commit settings and affected task state API->>Views: Publish settings and applicable chat/task changes API->>Queue: Release lock API-->>Person: Effective values, sources and updated-task count

runtime_guard_policy.resolve overlays registry defaults with Global, Conversation, Prompt and Run values. It ignores invalid/stale stored entries but rejects unknown or non-boolean explicit prompt/run values. bind preserves accepted retained-run policy instead of reading today's settings into an existing run. Current effective resolution also applies the registry's declared dependencies, such as research-proof checks.

The settings routes save a strict boolean or remove an override when enabled is null. Disable all atomically saves false for every registered global check; it leaves narrower conversation/run overrides separate.

The completion-structure preference has a narrow conversation update path for already queued chat tasks. Eligible tasks are unarchived, still queued, have no current attempt and have never had an attempt. A cleared attempt pointer alone does not make retried work eligible. The task and its live lane must belong to the conversation. Only this check's policy/source fields change; submission identity and unrelated accepted context remain intact. Each affected task gets a policy checkpoint and its lane version advances. Other check settings do not use this special queued-task rewrite, and a global change does not rewrite accepted tasks.

Controller RAM requires the native, settings and task stores to share one hub. The callback runs in its atomic authority transaction under the dispatch/revoke fence. Standalone SQLite holds settings/task locks, attaches their databases to the native connection and uses an immediate writer. Lock order starts with the task-queue lock, then any run ownership, settings/task locks and the writer. Notifications occur after commit; a storage failure cannot authorize a partial global Disable all operation.

Override a current run and use its domain recovery

sequenceDiagram actor Person participant API as Run route participant Authority as Authority participant Resume as Guard strategy participant Execute as Execution participant Views as Views Person->>API: Guard value and revision<br/>with optional strike identity API->>Authority: Apply correlated override alt Another worker owns progression Authority-->>API: Save policy for the<br/>next operation boundary else Route claims run ownership API->>Resume: Bind policy and<br/>invoke domain strategy alt Stop or explicit Pause applies Resume-->>API: Keep cancellation or pause else Candidate proved unexecuted Resume->>Execute: New claim and operation ID<br/>with original proposal Execute-->>Resume: New receipt through<br/>ordinary checks else Relevant retained completion Resume->>Resume: Validate retained evidence locally else Other strategy or next decision Resume-->>API: Return declared resume action end API->>Authority: Save state API->>Views: Publish retained outcome<br/>or running trace status API->>Authority: Release ownership end API->>Views: Refresh policy and settlement projections API-->>Person: Policy, status and resume action

PATCH /api/agent/native/{request_id}/agent-checks/{guard_id} carries the observed policy revision and optional strike/authority identity. The shared authority owner rejects stale correlation and stopped work before applying the native override. If the route cannot claim progression, the active worker adopts the saved revision at an operation boundary. The API response's resume action makes that distinction visible.

guard_strikes.resume_override honors Stop and explicit Pause before resuming anything. A stale model-decision identity or new amendment invalidates the saved resume candidate. Redispatch requires an exact retained invocation whose receipt proves executed=False, no possible remote effect and no unresolved unknown outcome. It assigns a new call and operation identity, retaining the original rejected receipt and journal group. Normal admission, permissions and current execution policy still apply.

Other strategies can resume a dependency branch, reevaluate a direct/retained completion, or leave normal model progression as the next action. The route itself does not request inference, but a permitted redispatch can perform an operation. Changing a guard is not equivalent to merely changing a presentation preference.

Reevaluate an exact retained answer atomically

sequenceDiagram actor Person participant API as Completion-only override participant Run as Owned retained run participant Tx as Policy and state transaction participant Views as Trace, chat and current run Person->>API: Exact decision ID and run or conversation scope API->>Run: Claim progression and verify partial candidate API->>API: Build lightweight retained adapter and buffer observations API->>Tx: Begin authority transaction Tx->>Run: Recheck lease, Stop, amendments and candidate identity opt Conversation scope Tx->>Tx: Save preference and eligible unstarted task policy end Tx->>Run: Record override and reevaluate retained evidence Note over Tx,Run: Remaining rejection stays partial, no worker is launched Tx->>Run: Save resulting native state Tx-->>API: Commit API->>Views: Flush observations and publish retained output API->>Run: Release progression ownership API->>Views: Normal settlement and update notifications API-->>Person: Resulting status and zero additional model calls

The compatibility route PUT /api/agent/native/{request_id}/runtime-guard requires the exact relevant partial candidate, structure-check feedback, no pending operation, no new amendment and no cancellation/tombstone. It rechecks those conditions inside the transaction. RAM retries reload state through the validated lease; buffered observations are cleared and rebuilt for each attempt so rolled-back attempts do not appear as accepted events.

retained_context restores a lightweight AgentLoop adapter around existing state, catalog, budget accounting, authority, Memory/KV/HTTP bindings and observability. It constructs no model client. The transaction records the run override, optionally changes the conversation preference and eligible queued tasks, reevaluates retained evidence and saves the native state. If evaluation would leave correction feedback with status running, this route keeps it partial: it has not launched a worker to service a new decision.

After commit, publish_retained uses ordinary publication, completes the trace, updates the existing conversation and refreshes the current-run projection. Queue settlement advances only when native truth is actually terminal. A publication failure after commit is not rollback of the accepted policy/state transaction. The existing native Resume path can also try local retained-answer recovery before deciding whether ordinary work must continue.

Source and validation boundaries

The two central modules are guard routes and retained final responses. Collaborators are the policy resolver, authority correlation, guard recovery and the SQLite/RAM queued-task policy writers. Each remains the owner of its existing transaction or execution boundary.

Preservation fixtures cover final text selection, stream interruption, stale intent, receipt-backed acceptance and missing/invalid declarations. API fixtures cover scopes, prepared snapshots, stale decisions, zero-inference reevaluation and honest partial outcomes. Guard-policy fixtures cover atomic Disable all, revision conflicts, pause ownership, uncertain-effect protection and redispatch with a new receipt. These tests use scripted providers and isolated stores; their results are separate from any live workload claim.
